chunks: Ali, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said:

I asked him about the wife who dies before she is entered into (consummated), or the husband dies before he enters into her. So he said: Whichever of the two dies, for the woman is half of what was obligated for her, and if it was not obligated for her, then there is no dower for her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dower if the husband or wife dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, clarifies the financial rights of a wife in the specific scenario of death prior to consummation (dukhul), a key distinction in Shia fiqh from the general rule of half-dower for separation. It establishes that the dower is halved only if a specific amount was stipulated; otherwise, no dower is due, reflecting the principle that the full dower is contingent upon the completion of the marital bond's primary physical aspect. This ruling underscores the legal precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding the conditional nature of marital financial obligations.
